Then:
$$\int -3\cdot\text{atan}(3x)\,dx = \int -\text{atan}(u)\,du$$

By integration by parts:
$$\int -\text{atan}(u)\,du = -\int \text{atan}(u)\,du$$

Since $\frac{d}{du}\text{atan}(u) = \frac{1}{1+u^2}$, we get:

$$\int \text{atan}(u)\,du = u\cdot\text{atan}(u) - \int \frac{1}{1+u^2}\,du = u\cdot\text{atan}(u) - \text{atan}(u)$$

Therefore:
$$\int -\text{atan}(u)\,du = -u\cdot\text{atan}(u) + \text{atan}(u)$$

**Step 4: Substitute back**

With $u = 3x$:
$$F(x) = -3x\cdot\text{atan}(3x) + \text{atan}(3x)$$

<answer>**-3*x*atan(3*x) + atan(3*x) + C**</answer>
